open_obligations: Note Arnesen et al.'s judge is fine-tuned on human judgements, Khan et al.'s is not.
Note training-based versus inference-time debater improvement.
Check that both use the same correct-answer versus best-distractor framing.
in.other_title: Stronger trained debaters yield +4 points judge accuracy; no effect for consultants
in.rationale: Khan et al. report judge accuracy correlates strongly with debater Elo when debaters are optimised at inference time. Arnesen et al. report that training debaters with self-play DPO is associated with 4 points higher judge accuracy (p < 10^-6) on QuALITY-HARD, with the judge never trained on these debaters' transcripts; both use GPT-4-Turbo-based judges on hidden-passage QuALITY.
in.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: whether stronger debaters yield higher LLM judge accuracy on hidden-passage QuALITY

Check whether calculator tools for agents change the capability ordering.

in.rationale: Khan et al. report judge accuracy rises with debater aggregate Elo in QuALITY self-play debates with a GPT-4-Turbo judge. Sudhir et al. say they reproduce this with new metrics: in Debate, higher Expected Agent Score goes with higher ASD on GSM8K with a gpt-4o-mini judge and five agent configurations; dataset, judge and metrics differ, so magnitudes are not comparable.
in.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether debate's truth-favouring signal strengthens as debaters become more capable

open_obligations: Check the size of the judge-accuracy gain in both studies before treating this as support

in.rationale: Khan et al. find judge accuracy rises with debater Elo; the authors explicitly report rough agreement, with a smaller and less consistent effect, mainly on extractive tasks.
in.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Positive relation between debater persuasiveness (Elo) and judge accuracy

open_obligations: Compare effect sizes: Arnesen et al. report a 4-point judge-accuracy gain from the SFT model to the final DPO model (p8 L23-25), while Khan et al. report trends against aggregate Elo
Confirm both studies measure debater skill by Elo-style win rates on QuALITY-HARD questions with hidden passages
Check whether Khan et al.'s trend holds for their GPT-4-level debaters, which Arnesen et al. call ambiguous (p10 L16)
in.other_title: Arnesen et al. find Khan et al.'s debater-skill/judge-accuracy trend persists with debate training
in.rationale: The authors explicitly say their training result matches the trend Khan et al. found with inference-time optimization (best-of-N, critique-and-refinement). How debater skill is raised and which judge is used both differ, so this corroborates the direction of the trend, not its size.
in.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether stronger debaters yield more accurate judges in information-asymmetric QuALITY debate; holds for training-based optimization with one fine-tuned LLM judge

open_obligations: Check the EAS-ASD slopes for the Debate configurations in Table 1 and Figure 2 and whether the trend is statistically significant with only 100 questions and five agents

in.other_title: Sudhir et al. find higher-EAS debaters raise ASD on GSM8K, matching Khan et al.'s persuasiveness result
in.rationale: Khan et al. report that judge accuracy rises with debater persuasiveness (Elo) on QuALITY; the authors report the analogous positive EAS-ASD trend for Debate. They call it a reproduction, but dataset, metric, judge and asymmetry (tools instead of hidden text) all differ, so it is recorded as SUPPORTS rather than REPLICATES.
in.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether more capable or persuasive debaters make debate favour the true answer more; holds for Debate in this small GSM8K setup.

open_obligations: Check whether 'better models' in the citing passage refers to stronger judges, stronger debaters or both, since Khan et al.'s Elo result concerns debater persuasiveness
Check that the citing paper's flat debater Elo is not in tension with Khan et al.'s finding that more persuasive debaters raise judge accuracy
Confirm the QuALITY subset in the citing work is comparable to Khan et al.'s QuALITY questions
in.other_title: Engels et al. find debate judge Elo rises with capability, consistent with Khan et al.
in.rationale: The authors explicitly say their observations are consistent with Khan et al. Khan et al. report judge accuracy rising with debater persuasiveness (Elo), whereas the citing result is about judge capability rising with general Elo while debater Elo is flat, so the agreement is at the level of 'better models help the judge' rather than the same variable.
in.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether debate judge accuracy improves as stronger models are used; holds for prompted LLM judges and debaters without training

open_obligations: Check Khan et al.'s limitation that RLHF debaters may resist lying.
Note that inference-time selection may not find strategies that training would.
Check whether the strongest debaters are strong enough to count as near-equilibrium.
out.other_title: Undiscovered dishonest strategies could break debate at Nash equilibrium
out.rationale: Michael et al. warn that strong dishonest strategies may exist that their human debaters did not find, and that testing needs more optimisation pressure, likely with AI debaters. Khan et al. optimise LLM debaters for persuasiveness and report judge accuracy rises with debater Elo; optimisation is inference-time (best-of-N, critique-and-refinement) and debaters are RLHF-tuned with an honesty propensity.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether more optimisation pressure on debaters keeps judge accuracy high, for LLM debaters on QuALITY with an LLM judge

text: Running self-play debates for each tournament debater on separate questions (TL) with a GPT-4-Turbo judge, the paper reports a strong correlation between judge accuracy and debater aggregate rating: as debaters are optimised against win rate (judge preference), judge accuracy improves. The authors state this suggests training models to win debates may produce more truthful outcomes and provides weak evidence that debate produces truthful information under optimal play.
title: Self-play debate: judge accuracy rises with debater aggregate Elo (persuasiveness)
